title: Advanced sulfur-functionalized highly porous carbon for efficient diclofenac sodium adsorption in aqueous systems
content: Softwood residues were converted into highly porous activated carbons by ZnCl2 activation, with and without sulfur functionalization, followed by ball milling. Sulf@AC and NonS@AC exhibited specific surface areas of 2550 and 2346 m2 g−1, respectively. Sulfur functionalization increased the ID/IG ratio from 1.68 to 1.84, and XPS confirmed the incorporation of thiophenic and oxidised sulfur species. XPS quantified the surface sulfur content of Sulf@AC as 1.81 at%. Sulf@AC showed faster DCF uptake and consistently higher adsorption performance under the investigated conditions. The pseudo-second-order model provided the best statistical description of the kinetic data, whereas the Liu model gave the best equilibrium fit at 25, 35, and 45 °C. Interpretation of the equilibrium behaviour considered the experimental isotherm profiles together with the fitted parameters and their uncertainties. In a multicomponent synthetic effluent, overall UV-vis spectral-area removals reached 92.7% for Sulf@AC and 89.9% for NonS@AC. The combined results demonstrate that sulfur functionalization, together with a highly developed porous structure, produces an efficient and reusable carbon adsorbent for DCF-containing waters.
